title: Microsoft 365 admin center: Microsoft Copilot usage report for GCC High and DoD
summary: Hold: the statement that the report takes no action on users is broader than Microsoft's documentation supports. Learn describes built-in organizational messaging that sends user notifications; remove the blanket assurance rather than assume that capability's government-cloud availability. The roadmap facts, concealment setting and Graph operation are supported.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk and impact
claims.claim: The report only reports activity, takes no action on users or content, and end users see no change.
claims.quote: You can identify and address Copilot adoption gaps in your organization by using the Organizational Messages feature that's built into the Microsoft Copilot usage report. This feature sends notifications directly to the users you need to reach to increase usage and adoption.
claims.fix: Replace the Autonomy & actions bullet with 'The roadmap describes activity reporting; it does not state whether organizational messaging is available in the GCC High or DoD report.' In the risk rationale replace 'The report only reports on Copilot activity' with 'The roadmap describes Copilot activity reporting'. In the impact rationale remove 'end users see no change'. Do not assert government-cloud messaging availability from the general documentation.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; rendered controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The concealment setting is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Org settings > Services > Reports > Conceal user, group, and site names in all reports.
claims.quote:
In the navigation menu, select Settings.
Select Org Settings.
On the Services tab, select Reports.
In the Reports panel, uncheck the checkbox next to Conceal user, group, and site names in all reports.

claims.claim: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/reportSettings updates concealment using displayConcealedNames.
claims.quote:
PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/reportSettings
 displayConcealedNames | Boolean | If set to true, all reports conceal user information such as usernames, groups, and sites. If false, all reports show identifiable information.

claims.claim: The tenant concealment setting applies across Microsoft 365 usage reports, including Graph and Power BI reports, not just Copilot.
claims.quote:
By default, all reports hide user information such as usernames, display names, groups, and sites to help companies support local privacy laws.
This setting also applies to the Microsoft 365 usage reports in Microsoft Graph and Power BI
claims.fix: Change 'The one control Microsoft documents for this report's user-level data is' to 'A documented control for this report's user-level data is'. The briefing also correctly identifies role-based access, so avoid suggesting the concealment setting is the sole documented control.
